name: nik 0.1
trained: p8 = the live v4f + 20 min SFT (lr 2e-4, bs 16, accum 2, muon, ema 0.998) on sft29: the v4f mix (sft13) + Sky's reduce.py at 8% (the symbolic two-step) + the grounded-role family at 12% (Local-C: bind the numbers in a text to their roles, carry the intermediate) + iter 5% + frame 5% (the money scene) + 20k persona rows, with the gate-prompt filter. molab box 2, RTX PRO 6000.
note: Paired against the live v4f on the SAME 288 nested items (bench.py --nested-items): bench 75.0% -> 76.0%, reason 41/48 held, understanding 13/26 -> 18/26, math 96% -> 97.5%, persona 1.0, and the procedure ladder for the first time in the project at L1 12/12, L2 12/12 (produce the intermediate and carry it - every model ever built scores 0-1/12), L3 12/12, L4 7/12. The two-step ability is now real and the bare one-step is intact. Caveats, stated plainly: trap_check 8/12 against the live v4f's 9/12 (the persona rows cost one identity trap: 'mero bhai kati barsha ko?' is answered as if the model were the brother), and stress 60/103 against 63/103 - but the stress suite's prompts are verbatim in the training mixes (Local-A's leak audit: thousands of exact hits), so the stress number is not a decision-grade signal for any model, including the live one. The understanding probes are clean (0 exact hits) and move +5. The benchmark's word templates are held out of the training data by a test (nik/tests/test_roles_leak.py, nik/tests/test_frame_leak.py), so the held-out word family 0/48 -> 3 families off zero is capability, not memorisation.
